criteria.text: Patient is 50 years of age or older
Prescribed by or in consultation with a neurologist
Beta-amyloid plaques verified by PET scan or CSF testing
Documented brain MRI within the last year showing no localized superficial siderosis, fewer than 4 brain microhemorrhages, and no brain hemorrhages greater than 1 cm in the past year
Objective evidence of cognitive impairment at screening
Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) global score of 0.5 or 1
Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score between 20 and 28
Other known causes of dementia ruled out, including vascular dementia and Parkinson's disease dementia
Not taking concurrently with other anti-amyloid immunotherapies
No brain hemorrhage, bleeding disorder, or cerebrovascular abnormalities in the last 6 months
No significant systemic illness or infection in the past 30 days
Amyloid plaque has not decreased to <11 Centiloids on a single PET scan or <25 Centiloids on two consecutive PET scans
No unstable angina, myocardial infarction, advanced chronic heart failure, or clinically significant conduction abnormalities within 1 year prior to screening

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Kisunla (donanemab-azbt) Criteria Version 1: Original 10/7/2024; Accepted 11/15/2024; Effective 01/01/2025.

Approval criteria 1-9 and denial criteria 2-6 encoded. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria. The amyloid plaque stop thresholds are an ongoing-eligibility denial gate. Treatment should be initiated at mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage of Alzheimer's disease; stage is notes only.

ARIA: enhanced clinical vigilance during the first 24 weeks. Symptoms suggestive of ARIA require clinical evaluation, including MRI if indicated. Risk of ARIA, including symptomatic ARIA, is increased in apolipoprotein E ε4 (ApoE ε4) homozygotes compared to heterozygotes and noncarriers. Common adverse reactions include infusion reactions, ARIA-Edema, headache, ARIA-H microhemorrhage and superficial siderosis. Cautions and monitoring remain notes only.

Initial approval: up to 3 months. Reauthorization: up to 6 months if the ARIA mitigation protocol has been followed per FDA guidance and there is documented positive response, slowed rate of cognitive decline, and no adverse reactions. Duration and reauthorization remain notes only.
Quantity per source FDA label approved protocol: maximum 1400 mg (four 350 mg/20 ml vials) infused intravenously every 28 days; HCPCS J0175. Dosing and quantity enforcement remain notes only.
Leqembi and Aduhelm are same-class anti-amyloid alternatives, subject to their own criteria and separate evaluation. No oral step-therapy requirement is encoded.
